test_runs.selector: Row205 shared-manager and exact-task binding suite
negative_cases: Cross-project or cross-session refresh of an existing exact task binding fails closed.
An ended Goal tombstones only its own binding and disables retry.

test_runs.selector: Goal, installer-registry, fallback-authority, and release-channel regression bundle
negative_cases: The Goal manager cannot use a release registry or selector as the task binding authority.
The installer and shared Goal-recovery manager remain distinct lifecycles.

test_runs.selector: PowerShell syntax, Python lint, and whitespace validation
test_runs.command: PowerShell AST parse; .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff check tests/test_goal_recovery_multi_binding.py; git diff --check
test_runs.output: POWERSHELL_AST_PASS; All checks passed; diff check returned zero
negative_cases: No manager, helper, scheduled task, tunnel, installer, HIL, pointer, candidate, or Git action was invoked.
Only source parsing and bounded static/regression tests ran.

limitations: Row205 implemented and tested the multi-binding manager contract without registering, refreshing, tombstoning, or recovering a live task binding.
Row206 separately owns fixed retry ceilings, per-binding backoff, and manager kill-switch behavior.
The shared scheduled manager intentionally has no fixed Task ID; every actionable identity is read from an independently sealed exact-task binding.

The native verifier currently applies case-sensitive fnmatchcase to Windows locators. The lowercase source locator resolves to the existing mixed-case Goal manager file and is required by the row's lowercase *goal*.* authority glob.
